title: CIMD Lab: client ID metadata documents, both directions

glossary.definition: Client ID Metadata Document. The client's client_id is an https URL, and the authorization server fetches the JSON document behind it instead of requiring registration first.
An https URL with a path, no fragment, no query and no credentials. The document served there must repeat the same URL as its client_id.
The older way to avoid manual registration: the client POSTs its metadata and the server keeps a record. CIMD keeps no record per client up front.
A stranger chooses the document URL, so the server refuses private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses, redirects, oversize bodies and slow answers.
PingFederate is the authorization server and the lab is the client. Real PingFederate only; there is no mock of it.
The lab's own teaching authorization server accepts a URL as client_id, and a tester shows each way a document is refused.
